content: Hi — I'd like branch access to open a PR: the Tsirelson-tightness construction requested in the "Future work" header of Mathlib.Algebra.Star.CHSH (explicit saturating CHSH tuple + the least-constant statement), plus a couple of small floor-arithmetic lemmas. My GitHub username is stalex444. Thanks!

@Stephanie Alexander Mathlib no longer require branch access to open PR. Please review https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/how-to-contribute.html for how to open PR from a fork
Could you also tell us where you got the information about asking for permission?
Thank you — I'll follow the fork workflow from the guide. To answer your question: I must've pulled up some old instructions. Apologies.
@Stephanie Alexander would you point to the instructions you looked at so we can clean them up?

Sure-- I asked AI (Claude) to pull up the current PR process and it apparently still defaults to an old version of the instructions it was trained on from awhile back so I was inadvertently using an obsolete version. In addition, I looked at the request above mine in this chat and it seemed to confirm that I had the correct process. I did not notice that the message was several years' old, I just saw that the message was dated in the morning and thought it was current (from this morning, and not old).
Hi! I'm a software engineering student. I'd like to start with some small contributions - easy issues, missing lemmas, that kind of thing. Can I get write access? My GitHub username is rlwq.
This is no longer needed, see above
Johan Commelin has marked this topic as resolved.

Dagur Asgeirsson said:

see above

Maybe it would make sense to post a link to the new contributing instructions in this thread, since currently "above" is an example of somebody asking for an invitation and receiving one.

Also, I just noticed why I got confused by your "see above": Both the topics #mathlib4 > ✔ GitHub Permissions and #mathlib4 > GitHub Permissions exist. In the web client, they are not merged, but in the android app, they are.

Lol I'm a moderator here and I should be able to sort this out, but I can neither resolve the unresolved thread, nor move messages from the unresolved thread to the resolved thread (the error message says that I'm moving messages to the same thread).
